sources.entry: MyTouchbarMyRules - App to customize your Touch Bar as you want.

summary.one_liner: MTMR (My Touchbar My Rules) is a macOS app for customizing the MacBook Pro Touch Bar with built-in buttons, plugins, gestures, and custom scripted buttons configured through a JSON file.
summary.what_it_does: MTMR replaces the default Touch Bar contents with a user-defined layout stored in ~/Library/Application Support/MTMR/items.json. It ships built-in buttons for keys such as Escape, brightness, volume, and mute, plus native plugins for things like time, battery, CPU load, weather, currency, music, pomodoro timer, network usage, Dock apps, and upcoming Calendar events. Custom buttons can be built from static titles, AppleScript, or shell script output, and buttons can run key presses, AppleScript, shell scripts, or open URLs on tap, double tap, triple tap, or long tap. Two-, three-, and four-finger swipe gestures can trigger custom AppleScript or bash actions, and buttons can be limited to specific apps by app ID regex. The README also mentions a visual editor (MTMR Designer) and a place to share presets.
use_cases: customize MacBook Pro Touch Bar layout
add custom buttons to Touch Bar
show CPU, weather, or calendar events on Touch Bar
map Touch Bar buttons to scripts or key presses
configure multi-finger swipe gestures on Touch Bar
replace BetterTouchTool-style Touch Bar setup with a free tool
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the GitHub releases page
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask mtmr
Grant MTMR access under System Preferences > Security and Privacy > Privacy > Accessibility
Edit ~/Library/Application Support/MTMR/items.json to define your Touch Bar layout
notable: Fully configurable Touch Bar layout via a single JSON file
Native plugins for CPU, network, pomodoro, Calendar events, and Dock apps without shell scripting
Multi-finger swipe gestures with custom AppleScript or bash actions
Per-app button visibility using matchAppId regex
Third-party visual editor (MTMR Designer) mentioned in the README
caveats: Requires macOS Accessibility permission, without which Esc, volume, brightness and other system keys do not work
Weather plugin needs a user-supplied OpenWeatherMap API key and location services access
Some timeButton formatTemplate and locale values are noted as not working properly; yandexWeather is marked experimental
Designed for MacBook Pro Touch Bar models only
